We have developed a novel approach to pinpointing crucial collapse solutions associated with black holes using an analytical, statistical framework. By employing the Gaussian mixture model, we identified distinct groups of crucial collapse configurations and determined their prevalence. Additionally, we employed k-means clustering as a complementary technique to validate our results, thereby shedding light on the intricate structure of these configurations.

The freight cost dataset for the cargo shipping sector in 1966 was derived from the US Bureau of the Cddy and Communications and was categorized by ship size. The shipping volume, new and scrap values, and new construction data were sourced from the US Maritime Administration and the US Bureau of the Cddy and Communications and were segmented by mode which comprised cargo, tanker, and passenger cargo freight shipping. The shipping volume data are averages over the years 1963, 1964, and 1965. The new and scrap values, as well as new construction data are averages over the years 1960, 1961, 1962, 1963, 1964, and 1965.

The field of Information Security is heavily reliant on Web anomaly detection, 
which involves identifying irregular patterns in web data such as SQL attacks, 
malware downloads, and data breaches.  Despite the critical need for effective
Web anomaly detection, research in this area has been hindered by a lack of
coordinated effort due to the absence of standardised evaluation procedures.
Consequently, it is not feasible to compare the performance of various
detectors using a consistent set of metrics.  In this study, we conduct a meta-level
evaluation of Web anomaly detectors, examining their performance under a range of
standardised conditions.  We conduct our evaluation using a range of anomaly
detection algorithms applied to a diverse range of datasets.  We then compare
the results to a baseline model, and consider the impact of key factors such as
algorithm selection and feature engineering.  Our findings indicate that the
performance of Web anomaly detectors is highly dependent on the choice of
algorithm, and that feature engineering can significantly enhance detector
performance.  We also identify a number of potential research directions for
further investigation.

The early detection of gliomas, a widespread and often fatal type of brain cancer, is crucial for effective treatment and prognosis improvement. The segmentation of gliomas in brain MRI scans is of significant importance in both clinical diagnosis and cancer treatment planning. This study introduces a novel approach for accurately identifying and isolating gliomas in T1 contrast images. By employing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) combined with post-processing techniques, our method achieves highly accurate results. The proposed technique has been rigorously tested on over 300 brain scans from patients diagnosed with gliomas, yielding exceptional outcomes. The findings reveal a Dice coefficient of 0.8466 and a high F1 score of 0.8635, significantly outperforming previous methods in both brain cancer treatment and segmentation accuracy. This breakthrough has significant implications for the early detection and treatment of gliomas, and for the development of more accurate medical image analysis techniques.

We investigate the likelihood of observing triplons in various magnetic lattices. To do this, we first determine the critical temperature above which the magnetic ground state changes from a triplet to a singlet within a specific magnetic lattice. Next, we analyze the spin-wave spectrum of the same lattice and identify the frequency at which the third spin-wave excitation occurs. Finally, we convert the parameter of the frequency of the third spin-wave excitation to the energy of the tripton. This leads us to identify various magnetic materials where triplons are present at accessible temperatures and can be measured experimentally.

We introduce the concept of statistical convergence using an omega-deterministic sequence, where an omega-deterministic sequence is defined as a two-variable function γ from the natural numbers to the natural numbers, satisfying specific conditions. An omega-deterministic sequence is said to be statistically convergent to a limit l, relative to another sequence (x(n)) with natural number indices and real-valued elements, if the limit l equals the mean value of the sequence x(n) weighted by γ(n) across all natural numbers. The concept of statistical convergence through omega-deterministic sequences has far-reaching implications, particularly in terms of selecting a subsequence from (x(n)) with unique properties. The study also explores the relationship between various types of convergence, including statistical, asymptotic, statistical convergence through weighted means, and omega-convergence. As a result, new methods for determining the asymptotic density of a set or approximating its asymptotic density have been developed, leveraging the statistical convergence through omega-deterministic sequences.

This study develops two methods to solve the one-dimensional Rosenau equation using non-continuous finite elements and investigates the numerical stability of the time discretization schemes employed. The Rosenau equation, used to model two-way propagation and dispersion in media, is a more comprehensive version of the Korteweg-de Vries and Boussinesq equations, particularly suitable for wave propagation models. The equation is defined as:

The one-dimensional Rosenau equation is given by:

u_t = x \ part of the derivative u_{xxx} + \lambda u_x + \mu u_t u_x

The Rosenau equation is discretized in space using the non-continuous Galerkin method and a variety of time discretization techniques are examined. The stability of the resulting time-dependent schemes is analyzed. The results of the numerical simulations, using a non-continuous Galerkin approach and the $\theta$-method with different values of $\theta$, demonstrate that the scheme is stable if $\theta \geq 0.5$.

This paper introduces a compressible flow - incompressible fluid interactive PDE system, which incorporates a Navier - Stokes system for the compressible fluid and a Navier - Stokes system for the incompressible fluid, interacting through shared velocity and pressure fields. The interaction is achieved by imposing a velocity - pressure slip boundary condition on the compressible fluid's domain and a no-slip condition on its interface with the incompressible fluid's domain. The system is analyzed under a range of boundary conditions, including various combinations of Dirichlet, Neumann, and friction conditions. The authors establish well-posedness in the context of interactor theory, which is equivalent to a well-posedness result in the context of abstract semigroup theory. The key technical challenge is overcome by employing a new inf-sup approach, which is a standalone achievement and can be applied to similar interactor theory applications.

In this study, researchers observed the Wigner crystallization of charged excitons in van der Waals heterostructures made of MoS$_2$ and WS$_2$. By applying a magnetic field, they induced the phase transition and found the melting and formation temperatures to be influenced by the magnetic field in a predictable manner. The team also measured the magnetic field dependence of interlayer exciton magnetization and extracted the effective g-factor of MoS$_2$ and WS$_2$ excitons. The results demonstrate a simple method for creating charged Wigner crystals in van der Waals heterostructures with tunable properties.

The LAMOST telescope's medium resolution spectrum database contains over 3.4 million spectra. This study aimed to develop a calibration method for the radial velocity of the spectra in the MRS catalog. We utilized a novel approach, where the radial velocity of a star is determined by averaging the velocities of multiple spectral segments. This method was applied to the LAMOST MRS catalog, and the results were validated through comparisons with the CALIFA survey and the Gaia DR2 catalog. We also examined the relationships between the MRS catalog's radial velocity and other relevant parameters, such as signal quality, exposure time, and wavelength. Our analysis revealed a strong correlation between radial velocity and signal quality. Additionally, we identified a significant wavelength drift issue affecting the MRS spectra, which was found to occur primarily on the blue end of the spectrum.

The inverse scattering problem, a fundamental challenge in physics, involves reconstructing an object's properties from measurements of the electromagnetic wave it scatters. This task is notoriously difficult due to its non-linearity, and recent attempts using deep learning-based methods have made limited progress. This work demonstrates that a specific type of neural network, trained to solve a related problem involving narrow-bands, is highly effective in solving the inverse scattering problem across a wide range of frequencies. We attribute this success to the network's ability to generalize its knowledge of neural activation patterns across various frequencies, and show that each neuron in the network learns to identify features specific to different frequencies. Our approach offers a novel solution to the inverse scattering challenge, and our implementation provides a simple and efficient method for reconstructing the dielectric properties of the object.

Reliability engineering has seen significant growth in Enhanced Degradation Testing (EDT), which focuses on accelerating life testing by repeatedly measuring a product's sensitive characteristics. This paper introduces a new method, dependent on gamma distributions, for performing EDT. By employing the bivariate gamma distribution to model the measurements from two related sensors, the proposed approach takes into account the dependency between elements. It also develops optimal strategies for sampling sensor readings at different time points, and demonstrates the effectiveness of its parametric approach through examples and real-world data analysis.

We analyzed the three-dimensional anisotropic flow $v_3$ of pions and kaons up to midrapidity in 200 GeV Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions at different centralities to gain insights into the early system dynamics. By employing the MAAv3 framework, we found that tri-axial angular momentum and initial momentum anisotropies play a significant role in the development of $v_3$. Additionally, we determined that the system's anisotropic flow is influenced by the interplay between radial expansion and the anisotropic width of the initial state.

A unique interaction between an ICME and high-speed solar wind stream was observed on October 17, 2018, which enabled the investigation of the resulting plasma behavior and its relationship to magnetic fields. The data showed that the magnetic field strength within the ICME increased as it approached the interaction point, while the solar wind speed remained constant. Conversely, outside the ICME, the solar wind speed increased as its radius and distance from the Sun increased. Our analysis revealed a distinct, polytropic relationship between the plasma pressure and magnetic fields within the ICME, characterized by a polytropic index (gamma) of 1.5. Furthermore, we observed a similar relationship between plasma pressure and magnetic fields within the ICME, with a slight variation in the form of solar wind density. The magnetic field strength and plasma beta exhibited a unique correlation, which was not observed in the ambient plasma outside the ICME. The magnetic field lines were found to be more tightly coiled within the ICME compared to those outside.

This research examines the random waypoint mobility model, commonly employed in simulations to model mobile nodes in ad hoc networks. Initially, we derive the probability distribution function of a node's position, velocity, and acceleration, utilizing these results to establish an analytical model of the random waypoint protocol. Furthermore, we develop a Markov model to represent a node's sequence of visited waypoints over time, and investigate the connection between the random waypoint model and the random walk.

The analysis of $K^+K^-$ pairs revealed two distinct structures near $2m_K$, with the first occurring at $2m_\pi$ and the second at $2m_D$. This investigation focused on the latter as it's accessible through resonant interactions and is a crucial step in detecting a $K^+K^-$ bound state. By examining the $K^+K^-$ pair's invariant mass distribution in the c.m.s, we found that the first structure is a statistical anomaly, while the second is a genuine enhancement. This research laid the groundwork for a more in-depth study of $K^+K^-$ bound states, paving the way for future research.

The canonical D1S energy density functional is employed to derive the effective mass and inertial moment, accounting for the non-locality of the Hamiltonian in the presence of nucleonic effective bulk in low-energy nuclear systems. By considering the low-energy Fermi surface, the microscopic inertial moment is calculated, revealing that the inertial weight is approximately 0.75. The calculated inertial moment closely aligns with the empirical value.

The IBM Research abe corpus is a collection of 120,000 complex visual puzzles, known as exploration graphs, which simulate real-world scenes and require problem-solving skills for successful completion. To tackle these puzzles, we developed a novel approach, involving a sequence of hierarchical object detection and labeling, to simplify and solve the problems step by step. To facilitate learning and exploration, we designed new training and evaluation methods, incorporating a novel graph-based self-supervised learning technique to identify key nodes for efficient exploration. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, solving around 70% of puzzles, whereas the current best method can only solve around 40%.

This study examines how material discontinuities in the flow field impact the stability of weak solutions in hyperbolic conservation equations. Building on the concept of fractional smoothness, we investigate the stability of weak solutions under two scenarios: when the flow field is discontinuous and when numerical approximations of discontinuous flow fields yield piecewise-constant solutions. Our findings demonstrate that in the first scenario, weak solutions exhibit only power-law non-locality, whereas the second scenario yields solutions with logarithmic non-locality. Our results are supported by several examples and special cases, including scalar conservation equations, the Euler equations, and systems of conservation laws.

The branching ratio of the $B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{\mp} K^{\mp}$ decays has been determined using data from the LHCb experiment, specifically from $3 \mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity. This has been achieved by comparing it to the $B^0 \to D_s^- K^+$ branching ratio, allowing for more reliable $B_s^0 \to D_s^- K^+$ measurement. The results are branching fractions of 

$\mathcal{B}(B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{\mp} K^{\mp}) = (7.4 \pm 0.3 \pm 0.3 \pm 0.9) \times 10^{-3}$,
$\mathcal{B}(B^0 \to D_s^- K^+)$ = (3.87 \pm 0.40 \pm 0.19 \pm 0.18) $\pm$ $0.19 \times 10^{-1}$,
$\mathcal{B}(B_s^- \to D_s^- K^+)$ = (1.88 \pm 0.24 \pm 0.09 \pm 0.03 \pm 0.04) $\pm$ $0.03 \times 10^{-2}$.

These findings are consistent with previous measurements and other branching ratios

This study explores the uplink performance of cell-free massive MIMO systems operating in full-duplex mode, particularly with respect to spectral efficiency. To mitigate self-interference issues, a joint transceiver design is applied, incorporating a hybrid analog-digital beamformer and filter that combine analog cancellation and RF-aware digital processing to minimize interference. Our numerical findings indicate that systems can achieve high spectral efficiency even at high communication rates. Moreover, a performance comparison with time division duplex systems shows that FD systems can achieve higher efficiency by reducing pilot training overhead.

A recent advancement in differential privacy called the shuffle framework, holds significant potential for applications in privacy-preserving data analysis. However, a critical issue arises from the fact that the shuffle framework cannot guarantee that the data analyst is unable to link individual data points to their respective inputs, even though advanced techniques of differential privacy are employed. In an attempt to resolve this problem, a new method is presented in this study to strengthen the differential privacy of the shuffle framework through strict accounting. By utilizing a novel method of analyzing the entropy of the output distribution, the method provides strong protection against backward tracing, ensuring that data analysts are unable to link individual data points to inputs. Furthermore, the method is efficient and can be easily integrated into existing shuffle frameworks. In fact, it has been shown that the method is capable of achieving the same level of privacy as that provided by the original DP-shuffle framework while also reducing its analysis complexity by a significant margin.

OTFS is a communication system that employs a two-dimensional representation of the signal in the physical time and frequency space. This allows for a pre-coding scheme in time space and after OFDM-like transformation, the signal is transmitted on a channel represented in the frequency space. Due to its properties, OTFS is less sensitive to mobility and requires less computational resources for equal performance compared to OFDM. OTFS is an attractive choice for 5G and beyond due to its low complexity. In this study, the OTFS modulation and demodulation process are mathematically formulated, followed by a comparison with OFDM in terms of complexity. In addition, the OTFS system is analyzed for its ideal receiver performance, and the development of a low-complexity receiver for OTFS is introduced, which leverages the sparsity of the receiver signal.

Consider a discrete semigroup $S$ with a weight function $\alpha$ defined on it. The weighted convolution algebra $L^1(S, \alpha)$ is equipped with the operator metric. In this paper, we establish the strong convergence in this algebra to the Green's topology, where no ultrametric is present. Furthermore, we establish that $L^1(S, \alpha)$ is a Banach $X^*$-algebra if and only if $S$ is a group and $\alpha$ satisfies certain conditions.

Researchers have observed significant porosity in laser melt welding of thick aluminum plates due to the rapid movement of the melt pool, which results in a low temperature solidification boundary. To mitigate this issue, a conduction-mode laser spot melting technique was developed to create a deeper and wider melt pool. This study employed high-speed imaging and inverse heat transfer modeling to understand the melt pool's behavior. With the aid of inverse heat transfer modeling, the melt pool's temperature distribution and solidification front's temperature were accurately determined, revealing a temperature range of 100-300 degrees Celsius for the liquid- solid boundary. This finding suggests that the melt pool's temperature is primarily influenced by the heat conducted from the solid substrate, rather than radiation. Modeling results indicated that the melt pool's temperature is primarily influenced by the heat conducted from the solid substrate, which could be used to optimize the welding process.

This research focuses on a wireless energy transmission and mobile edge computing issue in public transport vehicles, where multiple vehicles provide wireless energy to multiple passengers through satellite and base station communication while offering computing services for battery charging. The paper formulates a combined energy efficiency and computation time minimization issue, where computing services are delivered via an integrated satellite and base station network with a smart reflecting surface. The paper first proves that the problem is non-convex, then proposes a DQA algorithm for solving it using the DQA framework. The algorithm also compares its performance to alternative approaches such as the traditional convex SCA algorithm and a baseline algorithm. The paper further extends the issue to a scenario with multiple public transport vehicles and a variable number of passengers, where each passenger has its own computing task, and develops an iterative algorithm to find the optimal solution. The algorithm also shows the performance comparison with the DQA approach.

We introduce a novel measure for quantifying the extent of either disjunctive or conjunctive structure within Boolean formulas, expressed in either disjunctive normal form or conjunctive normal form, which is proven to be computationally feasible. This is accompanied by an empirical analysis of real-world CNF formulas, revealing that, on average, approximately 74.5% of their constituent clauses are interpretably CNF.

This research focuses on employing topological methods to identify stable, dual systems that arise in ecological environments. We develop a method for generating all possible bistable configurations within a given, closed and dimensionally bounded space. Additionally, we present a method for generating specific bistable scenarios within the same setting, and validate these approaches through two real-world ecological examples.

For the first time, we have explored the effects of temperature, magnetic field, and strange quark mass on the structure of spin-aligned strange quark stars across varying conditions. Our research indicates that the speed of sound and the stars' size decrease as temperature and magnetic field strength increase. Additionally, we found that increasing temperature and magnetic field strengths result in more compact spin-aligned strange quark stars. These observations suggest that such stars may appear smaller than their counterparts without magnetic fields, magnetic field influence, and at lower temperatures. Furthermore, we have derived analytical equations for the radius and mass of spin-aligned strange quark stars across various scenarios.

The human brain's ability to integrate audio and video information is highly sophisticated, allowing us to seamlessly interpret and understand the surroundings. This phenomenon is crucial for advanced technologies such as augmented reality, virtual reality, and autonomous vehicles, which heavily rely on audio-visual perception. This survey provides an in-depth analysis of the current state of deep audio-visual association learning, exploring the core challenges and proposing innovative solutions to overcome them. We initiate by discussing the importance of audio-visual alignment, followed by investigating methods for learning audio-visual representations and integrating these representations within specific tasks. Finally, we highlight the challenges and offer insights for further advancements in this area.

This study examines the dependability of answers derived from linear sequencing issues, such as those found in Sudoku, by introducing a unique resolution criterion. Unlike traditional methods, our approach considers an instance as resolved when only specific positions, known as issue positions, contain exact matches. Theoretical analysis reveals that this definition is more precise in detecting minimal issue instances and enhances the durability of algorithms searching for these instances. Our investigation into the dependability of answers under random and controlled Bernoulli valuations shows that a large proportion of answers are accurate with a probability of at least 3/4. Furthermore, we have developed a probabilistic algorithm that can be used to verify the dependability of answers in these instances.

Theoretical analysis of mid-infrared vibrational spectra in superconducting NbN nanofilms has been conducted, accounting for the nanoscale nature of the films. The study reveals that the granular structure significantly influences the superconducting phase, leading to the appearance of unusual spectral features. These include the development of additional mid-infrared peaks and changes in the intensity of existing peaks and interpeak connections. The study further shows that the granular superconducting state exhibits a previously unknown transition state, characterized by a fluctuating superconductivity that is spatially inhomogeneous. This transition is sensitive to the nanoscale and can be detected through the analysis of the infrared spectrum.

We're examining the issue of navigating through time, where an agent moves from a given start point to a target location, with the requirement that the path does not alter at any given instant. The problem is relevant in scenarios such as navigating a dynamic environment with a persistent view, where an adaptive system can continuously update its route based on changing constraints. To address this problem, we introduce a new problem known as Temporal Consistent Path Inquiries, or TAPI, and study its feasibility in relation to a variant problem known as Temporal Consistent Path Finding, or TAPI*. We establish that TAPI is NP-hard, demonstrate the feasibility of a polynomial-time solution for TAPI*, and present a randomized algorithm to solve TAPI in polynomial time, with the result of proving that TAPI is computationally tractable.

Polyatomic radicals containing lithium have been underrepresented in studies, partly because many of these species have unstable structures and decompose rapidly, making them difficult to create and analyze through conventional methods. We have developed a novel approach to create and study polyatomic radicals in a stable form, utilizing laser-based molecular beam technology. This involves a two-stage deceleration process using a Zeeman microwave laser for the initial phase, followed by a second round of deceleration and finally, a velocity selection using a second laser. We have successfully produced and studied two new lithium-containing radicals, specifically LiCCl2 and LiCH2Cl, using this approach. Notably, our study has the first experimental measurement of these radicals' electronic ground state constants, specifically A, B, and C rotational values, which matched well with theoretical calculations. We have also observed that the lithium-related signal from these radicals persisted for up to 1 ms after they decomposed, suggesting that the lithium atoms from this process do not disrupt the subsequent analysis of these radicals.

The XRT Point Source Catalogue contains information about point sources detected during live-time observations by Swift-XRT using a tailored pipeline, focusing on transient events. Utilizing this pipeline allows for the detection of sources initially not visible in pre-flight observations with significantly reduced exposure times. We introduce a novel transient detection algorithm, which is now part of the XRT Point Source Catalogue and used to recalculate the catalogue. We provide an overview of the pipeline, discuss its performance and accuracy, and discuss challenges in accurately localizing transient sources. We also introduce a newly developed feature, the rapid transient response pipeline, which enables the identification of sources with extremely short exposure times.

We investigate the ground state of a spin-1/2 XY model with J1 and J2 interactions on a square lattice. This model can be represented by a plaquette valence bond state, which we analyze using a plaquette mean-field approach. We determine the thermodynamic ground state by considering all possible plaquette valence bond configurations and their associated energies. We also examine low-energy excitations by introducing single plaquette valence bond defects. We find that the XY model's ground state has a direct transition to a plaquette valence bond state for all ratios of J2 to J1. However, the model's ground state exhibits a phase transition when both J1 and J2 are less than their critical values, which are 0.0 and 0.5, respectively. We also observe that for ratios of J2 to J1 greater than 0.5, the XY model's ground state consists of a plaquette valence bond state with a period-2 arrangement of plaquettes.

This research introduces a data model that decomposes mutual trade by representing countries as nodes, and associates each node with its corresponding balance. By utilizing this model, we examine trade relationships between countries over time. Our findings are exemplified through case studies of trade interactions between the United States and China, France and Germany, the United States and Mexico, and the France and Mexico. Our analysis reveals a pattern where countries primarily export raw materials and import manufactured goods. Furthermore, we identify a notable trade surplus in balance values for the United States, a moderate surplus for France, and a slight deficit for Germany. In contrast, we observe the opposite pattern for China, with Mexico appearing as a net importer. Our research also indicates a correlation between a country's balance and its per capita GDP. By analyzing the trade dynamics between China and the United States, we discovered that the US has a trade deficit due to China's significant exports of energy resources. By analyzing the trade between France and Germany, we found that the primary trade deficit is attributed to Germany's exports of manufactured goods, while France's deficit is largely due to energy imports. In contrast, Mexico's trade deficit is largely the result of energy resources and manufactured goods exported by the US.

The most straightforward adjustments to classical $U(1)$ theory occur when considering noncommutative gauge theory, resulting in a modified action that is invariant under the $U(1)$ gauge group. This action is derived from a modified action for a charged scalar field proposed by Van Suijlekom. This study examines the $L_{\infty}$ structure of this modified action, focusing on the modifications required to the $L_{\infty}$ structure of the classical $U(1)$ theory. This is done by analyzing the $L_{\infty}$ structure of the classical theory, the modifications required for the new action to be invariant under the $L_{\infty}$ structure, and the modifications required for the gauge transformations to be well-defined within the new theory. This is done through the use of a novel algebraic framework, the Maecel package. This study also considers the modifications required within the context of the noncommutative gauge theory.

We establish a quantum analogue of the concept of path integrals and develop a novel quantum mechanism equalization process. This process empowers researchers to apply classical equalization techniques to investigate quantum systems, providing researchers with a method to analyze quantum mechanisms through a modified path integral framework. Our approach is demonstrated by applying this technique to the equalization of the additivity of the broadcast channel, resulting in a proof of its additivity using this revised methodology.

Individuals experiencing mental health disorders often exhibit distorted time perception. Our research introduces a novel approach to quantifying passage of time by developing a predictive model that forecasts when an individual is likely to acknowledge the elapsed time of a task or activity. This task-based formulation aligns with real-world scenarios such as completing homework, exercising, or engaging in household chores, making it a valuable resource for mental health monitoring. The proposed model utilizes behavioral features extracted from human interactions, including speed, movement, and inactivity. It provides timely, in vivo predictions of when individuals with and without a diagnosed mental health condition are likely to recognize passage of time.

This study examines how decision-making speed affects both the quality of decisions and their implementation in real-time, relying on data from a mobile app used for crowd-sourced tasks during the COVID-19 pandemic. Results demonstrate that faster decision-makers tend to produce better outcomes, and also reveal that decisions made more quickly are more likely to be carried out as intended. Notably, these findings are supported by decisions involving the allocation of tasks to specific workers, where complex trade-offs are involved, showing that faster decision-making is associated with greater task completion efficiency. These observations align with previous research from the psychology and economics fields, suggesting that decision-making speed can influence the quality of decisions, and also contribute to a better understanding of intricate decisions made in uncertain contexts.

This study examines how various equity definitions intersect and influence one another. We show that the first two equity definitions are linked through the short-horizon limit, thus determining the behavior of the first two equity definitions dictates the viability of the third. Our research indicates that the order in which the first two equity definitions are applied is insignificant; however, the timing of the second one is vital and can impact the resulting process of the first. Furthermore, we establish a connection between the third equity definition and the infinite-horizon infinite-discount case, and an infinite time window leads to an equity process diverging from the corresponding marginal utility process.

A new method for detecting parity-violating effects resulting from neutrino-nucleus collisions has been proposed. This involves utilizing trivalent lanthanide ions with embedded electrons that are sensitive to both electric and magnetic properties. These ions are initially magnetized in one orientation, and then exposed to the resulting neutrino collisions. A change in the ion's magnetic alignment can be observed via the shift in the ion's electronic spectrum, allowing for a measurement of the affected ion fraction. This method offers a high sensitivity due to its ability to measure the change in the ion's magnetic moment, which is approximately 4 orders of magnitude greater than traditional methods. This new technique has the potential to be applied in the RESONANCE experiment.

Our study explores the mass spectrum of both single- and double-strangeness hypernuclei, with atomic masses ranging from 6 to 8, using $\Lambda$ hyperons. In the context of chiral effective field theory, our calculations draw from the leading-order Lagrangian with $\Lambda$-nucleon-$\Lambda$ interaction terms. In order to facilitate the computation of double-strangeness hypernuclei, we employed the no-core shell model and the single-body density matrix method within a 16-dimensional Hilbert space for each particle number, with $\Lambda$ isospin components as the basis. Our results for $\Lambda$ separation energies in $\Lambda^8_X$ are compared with existing data, while predictions are made for the binding energies of previously unobserved hypernuclei, with a focus on $\Lambda^8_{\Xi^0}$ and $\Xi^8_X$.

As social media usage expands, concerns about social media privacy continue to grow, particularly with the widespread sharing of personal information on these platforms. Given the embedded nature of social media in people's lives, where social and online lives are increasingly intertwined, the need to protect privacy through technological means becomes more complex. This work presents the concept of MetaPriv, a privacy support framework that acts on behalf of users to protect their privacy on social media platforms. By utilizing control flows and proxying user requests, MetaPriv safeguards users from potential privacy breaches while interacting with popular social media platforms like Facebook and Twitter.

In a diffusion approximation for a specific family of branching processes influenced by random environmental fluctuations, we investigate the process of time to coalescence for a system of independent branching particles.  This time to coalescence is modelled as a point process, with a compound Poisson distribution considered as a direct alternative.  The compound Poisson distribution arises when the branching process mean behaves linearly with its variance, resulting in a rare event where multiple particles coalesce simultaneously.  In contrast, a compound Poisson distribution is required when the branching process mean is significantly larger than its variance, a rare occurrence in real-world scenarios.  The compound Poisson distribution's probability density function is calculated and a thorough analysis is conducted to compare the effectiveness of compound Poisson distributions with an alternative distribution proposed in a prior study.

We examine a model of a HC (homogeneous tree) featuring vertices with an unlimited number of spin values, thus diverging from models where spin values are restricted to 1, -1, or a limited set. This allows for a broader range of Gibbs measures, including an infinite set, that may not exist in other models. Our analysis confirms the existence of a two-parameter family of Gibbs measures, where one parameter represents the degree of continuity in variation across distances of 1, while the other parameter represents the degree of continuity in variation across distances greater than 1. This two-parameter family encompasses both translation-invariant and non-translation-invariant measures. Our findings also include a proof of continuity for the Gibbs measure, where we show that for a given freezing parameter, Gibbs measures exhibit continuous variation with respect to the interaction parameter.

We introduce a new catalog featuring the speed dispersion of 234,858 galaxies observed by LAMOST. Our analysis utilized the application of the two-dimensional Fourier method to the velocity space within the radial distance of 0.4R90 from the galaxy's center. The results were validated through comparisons with existing catalogs of Galaxies in the Mvir and Galus. The resulting catalog is accessible via the LAMOSTDR7 website at http://www.amu.org.cn/lamostdr7/.

We have developed a new method, the analytic reaction relativistic coupled-cluster method, to calculate nuclear disintegration rates and assess its effectiveness by comparing it with established models. Our analysis focused on disintegration rates of various isotopes in indium, and we found that the model performs well when considering precise calculations, but in less detailed calculations, it shows improved accuracy compared to non-relativistic models. However, when incorporating relativistic effects in less precise calculations, they lead to underestimation of disintegration rates. Our research also showed that the model can accurately predict the pattern of stable isotopes in a specific nucleus, and it identified a previously unknown stable isotope.

A novel family of states, called Graph States, has been created by combining quantum information theory and graph theory. These states' classification based on their entanglement properties yields a rich, diverse minuscule group of possibilities. Conversely, a significant, nearly exhaustive set of states, known as the stabilizer states, has also been created by extending the concept of Graph States. These states' classification based on their entanglement properties is characterized by the signs of the principal minors of the inverse of their correlation matrices. Interestingly, a significant, dense portion of the possible pure states, making up an infinite, dense subset of the states, has classification based on pure 2-generated matrix determinants.

A well-established principle in the study of linear algebraic groups asserts that a specific subgroup, known as the stabilizer of a point, within a larger group is itself a complement to the kernel of the group's action. This equivalence has significant implications for the existence of transversals, a concept central to computational complexity theory, particularly in the context of group actions over finite fields. Our present work provides a straightforward criterion for determining when a specific subset of a group is capable of supporting transversals through its action on a particular set. This breakthrough offers a more accessible and efficient approach to identifying group actions with transversals, and has practical applications in the study of group actions over finite fields.

In cloud computing, resource heterogeneity is prevalent and poses difficulties for accurately predicting performance based on specifications alone. This means that predicting the optimal resource configuration for tasks like video transcoding becomes increasingly challenging. To address this issue, we propose a simulation approach that can help determine the most suitable cloud resources for video transcoding. This task is often required for big data analytics and our proposed simulation is designed to minimize the simulation time while achieving accurate results. To achieve this, we developed a simulation model that is based on a mathematical framework. This model is based on a new mathematical function derived from experimental data, which describes the relationship between the specifications of virtual machines and their corresponding performance. To further optimize the simulation process, we developed a new scheduling algorithm. This algorithm is based on a genetic algorithm, which uses a new fitness function to search for the optimal resource configuration. The performance of our proposed approach is evaluated through experiments conducted on a real cloud platform, which shows that our approach can achieve accurate results with significantly less simulation time.

In the context of the Elliott series, a cyclic pattern's total value can be expressed as $2\pi r$, where $r$ is the radius of the cycle. Given a set of cycles with radii $0<r_1<r_2<\dots$ encompassing all non-zero radii up to $R$, the total value of this set is represented by $2\pi (r_1+r_2+\dots)$. This study demonstrates that for any positive integer $n$, the quantity $2\pi (r_1+r_2^2+\dots+r_n)$ falls within a finite range, and provides a lower and upper bound. Furthermore, when $n$ equals $k^2$, where $k$ is a positive integer, the upper bound is found to be $\frac{\pi}{4} k^{-2} \log (R)$, and both the upper and lower bounds are found to be relevant in the case of a single cycle.

In the supercritical Gross--Pitaevskii equation, we examine the Morse index of the base state, a solution originally found by Gustafson and Reeve, to determine if it has any practical use. Contrary to the more common use of these states in nonlinear Schrödinger equations, where they serve as stable solutions, their Morse index is not useful for establishing stability as is typically done in lower dimensional cases. Instead, we find that the base state has a Morse index of n-1 in an n-dimensional space.

This paper introduces a comprehensive method for developing a structured framework in automated tools that controls for Type I errors, taking into account the evaluation of design quality for events, examples, and scenarios. The study builds upon prior research, specifically focusing on probabilistic methods for generating meaningful subsets of data, such as samples, instances, or scenarios. The approach outlined in this paper is applied in a working example to a previous research project, where we created a tool to automatically evaluate learning activity designs. The tool's effectiveness is demonstrated through a probabilistic analysis of 19 potential designs for two learning activities, each with two learning objectives, and three relevant variables. The results show that Type I errors are avoided, while Type II errors occur in approximately 12% of the cases.

The proliferation of AR devices and the growing interest in the Metaverse has driven a surge in demand for interactive 3D graphics, including virtual reality and augmented reality.  This demand has been hindered by limitations in hardware and network capabilities, including slow internet speeds and limited AR device capabilities.  To address these challenges, it is essential to optimize rendering for distributed environments.  This research presents Distributed HR, a distributed rendering system designed to enhance the performance of Metaverse experiences, including real-time rendering, low latency, and efficient network utilization.  We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed system through a case study of a Metaverse experience that showcases user comfort, visual clarity, and overall immersion.

In the field of music information retrieval, there is a growing need to develop technology that can automatically annotate sheet music. However, due to the complex nature of music representation, this task is more challenging than annotating audio recordings. To address this issue, we introduce a new metric called the alignment precision (AP) to evaluate the performance of music annotation models. This metric is designed to measure the precision of both annotation and alignment between annotated data and ground-truth music scores. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this metric, we conduct experiments using a large-scale annotated dataset of annotated MIDI files, resulting in the establishment of our "MIDI-Orchestral" dataset. Upon examination, this dataset reveals a significant number of common issues in performing this task, including the need for music alignment and the complexity of annotating complex musical expressions. To address these issues, we introduce two novel techniques: a hierarchical annotation model and a semi-supervised learning approach. The experimental results show that our proposed methods can achieve a significant improvement in alignment precision over traditional music annotation models.

In this research, we have developed a new method to mitigate self-interference in full-duplex systems, which do not require knowledge of the transmitter's signal power during the calibration process. By implementing a noise cancellation algorithm, our proposed approach effectively eliminates even the strongest radio-frequency interference at the receiver. To achieve this, we employ a combination of matched filter detection and a new method for estimating the transmitter's signal power. Furthermore, our proposed algorithm utilizes a novel approach to minimize the impact of an unknown transmitter's signal power, which results in a significant reduction in the amount of computational resources required. Experimental findings demonstrate that our proposed algorithm can achieve a signal-to-noise ratio of up to 110 decibels, even at high transmitter power levels. Moreover, our research highlights the benefits of using multiple antennas at the receiver to mitigate self-interference, thereby improving communication system performance. To this end, we develop a new method to combine signals from multiple antennas at the receiver, which achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of up to 120 decibels, even at high transmitter power levels. Experimental findings also show that our proposed algorithm can combine signals from up to eight antennas at the receiver, thereby achieving a signal-to-noise ratio of up to 120 decibels, even at high transmitter power levels.

During the cooling and solidification of a liquid droplet, it undergoes a transition from a smooth surface to a solid with distinct features such as bumps, folds, and cracks. The dynamics of this transformation can be complex, driven by the combination of capillary forces and the movement of the solid-liquid interface. Through a combination of theoretical modeling and experimental observations, it is found that the behavior of the solidifying droplet is influenced by the time it takes for the liquid to fully solidify, a process that is determined by the properties of the liquid and the solid. The study reveals that the liquid solidifies from the inside out, leading to changes in volume during the solidification process. The resulting dynamics of the solidifying droplet are highly nonlinear, leading to complex effects such as the bending of solidified material and the creation of invaginations in the solid. The study provides a detailed explanation of the underlying mechanisms responsible for these solidification features, offering a new perspective on the role of non-linear processes in the formation of solidified materials.

A crucial factor in the formation of stars and planets involves the interaction between gas and dust within protoplanetary disks. Infrared observations have provided valuable insights into disk properties, but the distribution and evolution of gas in these disks remain poorly understood. We have conducted a study using the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph on the Hubble Space Telescope to examine the physical and chemical conditions in protoplanetary disks. Our sample consists of 11 young stars with a range of ages from 0.5 to 10 million years, with a focus on eight stars that are known to be actively accreting. We have used the far-ultraviolet spectra to detect the presence of molecular hydrogen and its emission lines, with a particular focus on the distribution of its emission in the disk. Our findings show that molecular hydrogen emission is widespread in the disks of young stars, with a strong correlation between H2 emission and Lyman-alpha emission. Furthermore, we found that the H2 emission distribution is influenced by gas density and disk temperature, with a strong correlation between H2 emission and gas density. Our results also suggest that molecular hydrogen emission is a valuable indicator of gas density and disk temperature, with implications for our understanding of disk evolution and the formation of stars and planets.

A cutting-edge solution for 6G wireless network localization is the application of adaptive intelligent surfaces (IS). By leveraging the capabilities of IS, the physical structures such as antennas can be reconfigured to optimize signal propagation. In this research, a novel mmWave-based localization system is proposed, utilizing the characteristics of IS to enhance fingerprint establishment and adaptive beamforming for improved positioning accuracy. By adjusting the phase shifts of IS, the received signal fingerprint at each receiver can be maximized, minimizing the impact of line-of-sight (LOS) outages. A joint optimization framework is then formulated to determine the optimal beamforming weights at access point and receivers, maximizing localization precision. A two-stage algorithm is proposed to solve this joint optimization problem. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed adaptive beamforming scheme's ability to significantly enhance the localization precision compared to conventional methods.

We've discovered that a magnetic field can induce the formation of twisted, elongated regions within a mixture of oil and water containing specifically designed surfactant molecules, contrary to our initial expectations that the surfactant's inbuilt structure would remain intact. The opposite outcome occurred due to the surfactant's flexibility, allowing its molecules to adopt varied shapes that accommodate themselves within the curved interfaces they form and adapt to the changing local conditions.

The US electric vehicle market is shifting towards widespread adoption, driven by increasing adoption rates and rising sales volumes. As a result, the need for electric vehicle charging infrastructure is escalating, and numerous players are entering the scene. This study aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of EV charging station installation costs, installation practices, and financial viability, as well as the dynamics of the EV charging infrastructure value chain, and the financial dynamics of EV charging business models. The research is founded on a detailed examination of EV charging station installation costs, installation practices, and financial viability, and it explores the influence of EV charging infrastructure on profitability, investment, and value creation, and how different business models can coexist. The findings offer valuable insights for EV charging station operators, investors, and policy-makers seeking to navigate the EV market.

This paper presents a methodology for determining the most effective configuration of tie-breakers in multi-team tournaments, where teams are ranked based on winning and losing points, with tie-breakers used to resolve tie situations. We consider the scenario of n teams participating in a tournament where each pair of teams plays against each other, resulting in a total of (n-1)/2 matches. When two or more teams end up with the same score, tie-breakers are used to establish a definitive ranking. We aim to find the optimal tie-breaker system that maximizes the likelihood of achieving a valid tie-breaker outcome, where a valid outcome is defined as one that results in a unique ranking. We develop a method to calculate the probability of an invalid tie-breaker structure, and use this to derive the optimal tie-breaker system for any given number of teams. We also provide examples of optimal tie-breaker systems for a variety of scenarios, including the case of 11 teams participating in the 2018 FIFA World Cup.

In the context of the ${\mathcal N}=1$ superspace approach for $D=3$ space-time dimensions, a class of multiplets known as superconcurrent higher-spin multiplets ${\cal F}^{(n)}(Q^{\alpha i},\bar Q_{\dot{\alpha}^i})$ have been identified. These multiplets, which are linked to the original spinor superfield multiplet ${\cal F}^{(n)}(Q^{\alpha i},\bar Q^{\dot{\alpha}^i})$, have been found to be related to them through suitable differential operators in the superconformal group. This relationship has been further extended to derive expressions for correlations among these multiplets, which are essential for constructing conformal multiplets.

Recent advancements in natural language processing using machine learning models
have yielded impressive outcomes, but the complex, opaque nature of these models
raises concerns about their reliability and potential biases, particularly among
young users. To address these concerns, we conducted a study to gauge children's
ability to comprehend the underlying instructions guiding machine learning
algorithms and their effects on language processing. Our study revealed that
children aged 8-8.5 on average demonstrated a good understanding of model
functionality, but struggled to grasp more complex aspects. These findings suggest
that children possess valuable insights into machine learning's intricacies and
potential to collaborate with adults in developing more transparent and child-
friendly models.

This study offers an in-depth examination of the persistent success of 
Sutton and Barto's general reinforcement learning framework, highlighted by 
its widespread adoption in the development of deep reinforcement learning. 
At its core, the framework relies on the concept of an agent interacting with 
a discrete-state Markov process. Through a series of fundamental inquiries, 
we will uncover the inherent structure of this process, revealing its 
composition and how its components are interrelated. Building on this analysis, 
we will explore the implications of learning from this interaction.

We have developed a versatile on-chip platform that enables seamless transfer of photonic quantum signals between various states of freedom. By utilizing waveguides with tailored dispersion profiles, we can efficiently switch quantum states between different optical modes, including spatial, spectral, time, and polarization dimensions. The designed photonic circuit, comprising a waveguide with a resonant dispersion, can be easily fabricated using standard photonic wire technology in silicon or other materials. The versatility of our on-chip platform lies in its ability to transform quantum signals between different dimensions of freedom, thus offering a broad range of applications for quantum networks and quantum information processing.

We investigated the impact of various base pair mismatch combinations in DNA on the transmission properties of its genetic code. Using a two-probe scattering method, we discovered that mismatched pairs in DNA codons exhibit different levels of electronic conductivity. While some mismatches lead to reduced conductivity comparable to wild-type DNA, others cause a significant increase, up to 12 times greater. Additionally, we examined and compared the transmission properties of DNA's normal and complementary strands as well as their complementary pairs in relation to conductivity.

This paper introduces an innovative algorithm for accurately registering multiple 3D point clouds in a scene. The approach relies on a novel feature extraction technique, where features are grouped into clusters using the K-means method to reduce dimensionality and improve efficiency. Our method employs a cost function based solely on point coordinates to estimate camera movements, overcoming the limitations of traditional methods that require more complex, noisy features such as lines or circles to detect corners. Furthermore, our algorithm can operate in real-time, making it an ideal solution for real-world applications.

Our research examined the magnetic properties of Tb3RuO7 using multiple methods including muon spin relaxation, neutron scattering, and specific heat measurements. The analysis revealed that the Tb3RuO7 compound exhibits a spin-3/2 Ru chain structure with a disordered magnetic field caused by the interaction between Ru and Tb ions. The magnetic field's randomness prevents Ru moments from aligning in a consistent manner, resulting in a partially disordered state. The compound's heat capacity and magnetic susceptibility follow a power-law dependence, indicating a two-dimensional critical behavior. However, a close look at the neutron scattering data reveals that the Ru moments exhibit short-range ordering and rapid spin fluctuations. The muon spin relaxation data shows that the magnetic moments exhibit high spin dynamics. Our study provides a comprehensive explanation for the unusual properties of Tb3RuO7, which stem from its disordered internal magnetic field caused by the Ru-Tb interaction.

This study's primary goal is to investigate the optimality criteria for DC optimization problems. The research is conducted in two distinct scenarios: first, for constrained optimization problems where the linearized constraint functions are represented by a DC representation, and second, for general DC constrained optimization problems. The findings involve establishing necessary and sufficient optimality criteria for both cases using a specific quasi-subdifferential called the subdifferential of Asprea and Vastola. Additionally, it has been demonstrated that these criteria are equivalent to another set of quasi-subdifferentials, specifically the ones introduced by Ioffe and Quittet. The research also includes a specific example to illustrate the optimality criteria.

We explore the top-down construction of a $\text{AdS}_1/\text{CFT}_0$ in Type IIB supergravity by utilizing the D(-1)/D7 brane configuration. To achieve this, a specific top-down approach is applied to the supergravity action, by adding a topological term to the top-form potential, thereby avoiding the introduction of extrinsic curvature into the theory. The resulting background solutions reveal a class of $\text{AdS}_1/\text{CFT}_0$ spacetimes parameterized by the D(-1)-brane's worldsheet position, $x^7$. Furthermore, we identify a corresponding CFT realization, by introducing a gauge field on the D7-brane's worldsheet, whose $x^7$ position serves as the defining feature. The gauge field's behavior is described through the $\text{AdS}_1$ curvature radius, leading to the generation of a novel action, and we demonstrate that the background solutions are indeed the solutions to the conformal theory.

We're introducing a novel collision resolution method, Area Collisions, that allows for a smooth integration of complex characters and objects derived from vector-graphics artwork. Unlike traditional techniques, which primarily focus on convex shapes, our approach accommodates both convex and arbitrary shapes, significantly expanding its applicability to the vector field. Unlike rasterization, which scales images while maintaining their integrity, Vector-Brushes scale vectors to a pixelated format, resulting in a unique challenge for collision detection. To address this issue, we've developed a solution tailored to the needs of Vector-Brushes, detailing its underlying principles and algorithms, as well as a comparison with existing collision detection methods in games.

We introduce a novel Bayesian framework that unites control knowledge and deep reinforcement learning. This approach, called the Bayesian Controller, combines the predictive capabilities of a detailed robot model with the data-driven methods of deep reinforcement learning. The Bayesian Controller can be trained using either simulated or real-world data, and its unique feature is its ability to integrate prior knowledge from control principles. This allows it to efficiently utilize limited training data, resulting in faster convergence to effective control policies. Our experiments on robotic tasks demonstrate that the Bayesian Controller outperforms a standard deep reinforcement learning controller, and can also leverage simulated data to achieve comparable results to its physically-trained counterpart.

A widely used medical technique, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), relies heavily on deconvolution to produce detailed images, but this process can sometimes be hindered by the limitations imposed by measurement of signal recovery, which can lead to the loss of (minor) details. In an effort to address this issue, a new approach, known as differentiable deconvolution, has been proposed. This innovative technique employs an artificial neural network to perform the deconvolution process and has been found to not only maintain the original reconstruction's integrity, but also to enhance the quality of the resulting image, as evidenced by the use of a stroke perfusion MRI dataset which demonstrated improved assessment of stroke severity.

We initiate the third-order QCD calculation of ray functions associated with collinear zero-jettiness, leveraging our understanding of cross-section structure and the structure functions concept. For leading-color processes, we verify the validity of the cost-and-match principle through consistency with the known full next-to-leading-color result for $e^+ e^-\to$ jet$+$ jet$+$ X.

The power graph of a group, denoted by $G$, consists of all unordered pairs of elements that interact directly; this graph has been found to be chordal in specific cases such as groups $G$ with the power graph equal to their underlying graph or when $G$ has order $5$ or $10$. We now demonstrate that a group $G$ with a chordal power graph has an even larger structure known as the covering graph. Conversely, a counterexample has been identified in which a covering graph is chordal yet the underlying group $G$ does not possess a chordal power graph.

We've developed an algorithm to automatically isolate a target sound from its surrounding environment audio based on a given example of the target sound within that environment. Our approach relies on modifying the environment's sound characteristics through optimization to make the target sound more distinct from the other sounds. Building on the idea of policy gradient-based reinforcement learning, our algorithm finds the most effective way to isolate the target sound by iteratively adjusting the audio characteristics. To improve the speed of this iterative process, we've incorporated various techniques, such as data augmentation and faster optimization methods. Experimental comparisons with existing methods have shown our algorithm to yield higher quality sound separation in a range of environments.

This study explores how quantum observations, both standard and universal, behave in coherent states, and how these states maintain their separability in such observations. Building on previous research, we first established a framework for estimating the influence of conventional local quantum observations on coherent states, and now we're expanding on this concept to include the broader category of universal quantum observations. In doing so, we've identified specific criteria that must be met in order for coherent states to preserve their separability under the influence of these observations, and we've found that these conditions can be applied across a range of complex states, including the single-particle GHZ state and multi-particle Bell states.

We examined type C quasi-periodic oscillations in the low mass black hole X-ray binary H 1743--322 by analyzing its outburst data from 2002, 2010, 2013, and 2014 observations. Our investigation into the correlation between QPO frequency and outburst flux revealed a notable pattern in the 2013-2014 outburst, where QPO frequency increased as intensity rose. However, this pattern was absent in the 2002, and 2010-2014 outburst data. Our analysis suggests that the 2013-2014 outburst experienced a unique combination of high mass accretion rate and high disc radius, resulting in the observed frequency increase with flux. By modeling the accretion flow and infalling matter's emission, we determined that the accretion rate and disc radius in the 2013-2014 outburst were exceptionally high. Our study supports the notion that the Keplerian disk is truncated at low mass accretion rates, only extending to smaller radii at high rates, and that the observed QPO frequency is limited by the innermost Keplerian disk orbit.

This research introduces a framework for query processing on e-governance data, 
which is essential for developing a flexible and reliable search engine system 
across multiple data sources. We provide a methodology to optimize the use of 
publicly available natural language queries and translate them into SQL queries 
that can be executed against the underlying government database systems. Our 
approach is based on a public-domain framework that can be utilized by e-governance 
providers and users alike, aiming to increase the search engine efficiency and reduce 
the query execution costs.

Recent breakthroughs made by the EAGLE cosmological simulations have revealed a significant discrepancy between simulated and observed baryon masses in galaxy clusters. To better understand this difference, researchers analyzed the simulation results and found that a substantial portion of the missing baryons can be attributed to underdeveloped galaxies within small satellite systems. These satellite galaxies experience limited growth due to their small sizes and weak interactions, resulting in reduced baryon content compared to their more massive counterparts. As a result, a substantial amount of baryons are being stripped from the satellite galaxies, contributing to the observed deficit. Interestingly, a recent study of the Coma cluster found evidence of a similar phenomenon, with smaller galaxies showing a significant reduction in their gas content. To further investigate this effect, researchers explored the simulation results and identified a population of "missing" galaxies that are thought to be the source of the missing baryons.

Given an integer $k$ and a non-intersecting curve $\mathcal{C}$ within a rectangle $R$, we aim to find all the dividers of size $\leq k$ that start on $\mathcal{C}$. A divider is defined as a chord of the curve's interior where the endpoints touch $\mathcal{C}$ and the curve's interior lies between the endpoints and the dividing line. Our algorithm to find and locate the dividers of precise size $k$ has a time complexity of $O(nk^2)$ and to locate all the dividers of size $\leq k$ has a time complexity of $O(nk^3.3145)$. This is an improvement on the previous time complexity of the second task, which was $O(nk^4)$ time.

We have analyzed the recent spectroscopic data of 16 post-starburst and 10 Balmer-strong galaxies from the SDSS, focusing on their cores.  These galaxies were selected based on specific criteria, including the presence of narrow Balmer lines and a lack of emission in certain HII line transitions.  Our analysis revealed distinct categories of galaxies, including transition types such as post-starburst and transition types such as Balmer-strong, as well as a new type of transition, Balmer-strong post-starburst.  Our findings indicate that the cores of these galaxies are experiencing a decline in their Balmer line fluxes, a trend that is most pronounced in post-starburst galaxies.  These results suggest that the cores of Balmer-strong galaxies may be experiencing a change in their star formation dynamics, possibly due to the presence of a new young stellar population.  This new information provides new insights into the nature of Balmer-strong galaxies, a type of object that has previously been poorly understood.

In reconfigurable wireless networks, a crucial task for the scheduler is to assign radio resources to individual user connections in a manner that respects specific quality-of-service (QoS) requirements while optimizing resource utilization. A novel approach to this problem is presented in this paper, which frames the task as a continuous control issue. A proposed solution involves a two-part control policy: a performer, which determines the optimal radio resource at a specific time, and a critic, which forecasts the QoS consequences of individual resource assignments. These predictions are informed by a dynamic QoS model that takes into account the impact of resource allocation on individual users. A performer-critic learning strategy is then applied to train the control policy, which is evaluated through simulations using a dynamic wireless network scenario. Results demonstrate that the proposed scheduler surpasses traditional scheduling techniques in terms of both QoS performance and energy efficiency.

This research introduces a novel quality assessment model for terms, which will be utilized in post-editing tasks. As bilingual projects increasingly adopt project-based collaboration, the need for post-editing at the sentence level has been adequately addressed through previous models. Nevertheless, the efficient correction of terms remains an underexplored area of study. Our proposed approach integrates a model into the post-editing workflow to enable human editors to prioritize the correction of low-quality terms. By incorporating a term quality assessment model, we achieved substantial improvements in both system output and editing effort efficiency in two distinct domains.

We calculate the shadow radius of a star with a Schwarzschild-like metric embedded in de Sitter space. By linking this metric function to the shadow radius, we establish a connection that relates the (dimensionless) shadow radius to the star's mass. This relationship can be approximated by an equation involving a universal constant, known as the shadow radius constant. This constant is linked to the dimensionless Schwarzschild radius and the shadow radius, and its value is estimated to be approximately 0.25 with an error margin of 0.05. This estimate is consistent with previous findings from flat and anti-de Sitter spaces, and it can be used to estimate the mass of a Kerr-de-Sitter black hole based on its equatorial shadow.

This research introduces a newly formulated set of relativistic fluid dynamics equations, suitable for computational modeling of complex fluid phenomena in high-energy physics. The key advancements in this formulation include a novel approach to conserving baryonic number, a generalized mass tensor, and a specific method for resolving relativistic constraints. This formulation is applied to a two-dimensional Cartesian space with uniform grid resolution in both x and y dimensions, enabling the use of finite differences to discretize the relativistic effects. The derived system of finite difference equations is based on the conservative formulation of the relativistic Navier-Stokes equations, ensuring baryonic number conservation and potential extension to conserve charge and other quantities as well. The paper also explores the relationship between the new formulation and the conventional relativistic hydrodynamics equations, as well as its application in numerical simulations of fluid dynamics.

This paper aims to introduce a new type of fractal polynomial on the Sierpińsky gasket for each dimension between two specified numbers, and explores basic properties of these polynomials.

Artificial intelligence's visual inquiry form, which involves generating and manipulating images, presents unique opportunities and challenges for AI alignment. Directing visual inquiry offers benefits such as assessing an AI's alignment through its creative capabilities, as well as identifying and mitigating potential limitations in its ability to generate images. This study presents a framework for directing visual inquiry, which involves a generative AI selecting and arranging visual elements within a predefined grid. The study's key contribution is an adaptive AI system that can be scaled up to tackle the creative problems presented by visual inquiry. The study also defines and explores the concept of visual inquiry and its potential for directing AI behavior.

The supernova-driven mechanism is a theoretical model proposed to explain the discrepancy between observed galaxy density profiles and the predictions of the CDM model. In this approach, supernovae explosions are thought to have replaced dark matter in the outer regions of galaxies through repeated bursts of supernovae in the last 500 Myr, which have reduced the dark matter density in these outer areas to a significant degree. In order to evaluate the potential of this scenario, we have analyzed the supernovae required to alter the dark matter density in this way, and determined the conditions under which this model could be plausible. We have also considered the constraints imposed by the observed supernovae rates, and the constraints imposed by the observed distribution of galaxies in the nearby universe. Our results indicate that the supernova-driven mechanism is not a viable explanation for the cusp-core anomaly in the majority of spiral galaxies, but may be a partial explanation for a small subset of dwarf galaxies.

For a long time, researchers have been trying to find ways to convert higher-order proof systems into first-order logic. This is particularly challenging in the case of higher-order sequent calculi, which are used in proof assistants, despite the availability of many rules for derived rules. The process of extracting these rules, however, is complicated and often yields complicated first-order derivations that are difficult to understand. This paper builds on the work of a recent SAT-inspired approach, which aims to simplify the extraction of these rules by making them easier to identify. The proposed method can be used to create a clear and simple first-order sequent calculus for a particular proof system, which is demonstrated by applying it to a well-known calculus.

A replicator equation is a compartmental model of a single species that exhibits stability and historical influence.  In this study, a transformation is developed to produce replicator equations from Lotka equation solutions, which can be used to model species with neither stability nor historical influence.  These new equations are shown to be of a specific, symmetrical form, and the parameter space is analyzed to show the existence of unique, stable solutions.

This study develops a method to achieve normality and efficient estimation of the conditional expectation function in multidimensional settings using random forest techniques. Building upon established results for one-dimensional random forest models, a new class of multivariate random forest models is introduced, where each component forest is trained on a single-dimensional subset of the data. Under these new models, called forest combinations, the function values, prediction errors, and any given set of prediction residuals derived from these forest combinations are proven to be asymptotically normally distributed with a specific variance matrix that depends on the individual component forests' variances. Furthermore, this study derives the asymptotic variance of the forest combination estimator and demonstrates that it converges to the Cramer-Rao lower bound when its component forests converge to the target model. A numerical study demonstrates the benefits of combining component forests on performance and efficiency.

A novel approach to the electric vehicle charging problem within distributed power systems is proposed, focusing on efficient management of public charging facilities. By integrating a nonlinear optimization and transportation model, we develop a model to maximize revenue through variable pricing. This problem involves a network of electric vehicle charging stations and a larger power distribution system, which requires efficient communication between the two. To achieve this, we develop a two-layer solution framework, based on the alternating direction method of multipliers, to address the non-linear transportation problem and the larger power distribution system. To further reduce communication, a lower-layer solution utilizing linear programming is introduced, allowing the nonlinear transportation problem to be solved locally at each charging facility. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through numerical simulations, which show that our approach achieves comparable performance while significantly reducing communication requirements over existing methods.

Using density functional theory, researchers have employed first-principles calculations to study the structural, elastic, and electronic properties of $SmFeO_3$. The calculated lattice parameters and atomic positions in this study align closely with experimental results. An analysis of the density gradient along the $a$-axis in this study reveals that the $d$-orbitals of $3p$ electrons in oxygen and $4d$ electrons in iron are the most tightly localized, indicating $O-3p-I$ and $Fe-4d-I$ character in $SmFeO_3$. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the generalized Wigner-Seitz cell in $SmFeO_3$ is the largest among various perovskites, suggesting a high covalent bonding nature. Utilizing the generalized gradient approximation for exchange and correlation potentials, the study has calculated the elastic constants of $SmFeO_3$. The calculated values of these constants are in line with the requirement of mechanical stability, indicating that $SmFeO_3$ is mechanically stable. An analysis of the high-pressure phase has shown that $SmFeO_3$ exhibits a dynamic transition at 25 GPa, after which it becomes mechanically unstable.

The human microbiome plays a vital role in the regulation of metabolic processes, and a comprehensive understanding of its mechanisms is essential for unraveling the intricacies of metabolic disorders. A systems approach, utilizing a large database of known metabolic reactions, can facilitate the discovery of key genes and interactions that underlie this complex network.
